120	witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`.
121	
122	Stated with the witness clause on a *presenting Čech class* rather than on a datum,
123	because the datum layer is where the shifted-datum constructor (DAT-C GAP-1) is missing;
124	the two agree through `Pic0ChartLocusClass.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.
125	
126	## A convention this predicate INHERITS, and which a consumer must not misread
127	
128	The worksheets say "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`".  The witness clause here —
129	and the tree's `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`
130	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`) that it mirrors, and the GAP-6 dictionary
131	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (`DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:182`) that both rest
132	on — asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  It asks only for a `CurveDivisor` in the
133	class with vanishing `H¹`.  That is deliberate on the tree's side: the dictionary is an *iff*
134	against the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗ L)`, and that
135	condition cannot see effectivity or degree, so adding either clause would break the iff and
136	with it the openness route.
137	
138	Two consequences, both load-bearing:
139	
140	* the degree is supplied **externally**, by the chart-index constraint through
141	  `degAt_chartTwist` below: on a degree-zero `λ` the twisted class has fibre degree
142	  `m·d₁ − deg Z`, which the constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − g` makes `+g`.  It is *not* a
143	  hypothesis of this predicate.  (Until 2026-07-28 this read `−g`, and that sign made the
144	  locus empty for every `g ≥ 1` — see `degAt_chartTwist` and issue I-0514;
145	  `chartTwist_chartValue` now pins the direction by the kernel);
146	* effectivity likewise is not asserted here.  Where the *worksheet's* stronger reading is
147	  actually needed — the canonical-section normalization `h⁰ = 1`, and GAP-2 uniqueness
148	  (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`, which does take `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`) — the
149	  effectivity must be re-supplied at that point.  A lane that reads `IsSplitWitness` as
150	  already giving it will have a gap where it least expects one. -/
151	def IsSplitWitness {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
152	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) : Prop :=
153	  ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
154	      (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
155	      (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic),
156	    PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
157	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
158	      ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
159	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
160	            ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
161	                ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)
162	
163	/-! ## The twisted fibre family -/
164	
165	variable (C) in
166	/-- **The twisted family whose chart-membership `chartLocus` tests**: the plus class `λ`
167	shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family.
168	
169	This is the *class-side* half of `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`): where
170	`chartValue` twists the Abel class of a divisor family, `chartTwist` twists an arbitrary
171	plus class by the same two factors.  A point of `chartLocus` is precisely a point at which
172	`chartTwist` is realised by an effective divisor with no `H¹` — i.e. at which `λ` itself is
173	a chart value, after undoing the twist. -/
174	def chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : picEt C T :=
176	  lam * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m) * (sigmaFamily C Z T)⁻¹
177	
178	/-- **The degree ledger of the twist**: at every field point the twisted family has fibre
179	degree `m·d₁ − deg Z` when `λ` is degree-zero.  With the chart-index constraint
180	`deg Z = m·d₁ − g` this is `+g`, which is the degree at which an effective witness with
181	`h¹ = 0` can exist at all.
182	
183	**Sign discipline, and it was wrong here until 2026-07-28 (issue I-0514).**  `chartTwist`
184	must be the INVERSE of `chartValue`'s twist, not the same one.  `chartValue` is
185	`abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`), so recovering the Abel class from a chart
186	value means multiplying by `θᵐ` and dividing by `Σ` — hence `chartTwist` is
187	`λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`.  An earlier version applied the `chartValue` twist itself, giving fibre degree
188	`deg Z − m·d₁ = −g`; since `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))` forces `deg W ≥ g − 1`, that locus was
189	**empty for every `g ≥ 1`** and its openness was the openness of `∅`.  The comparison point is
190	`degAt_chartValue` at `n = g` (where the chart index is calibrated and `chartValue` lands in
191	`pic0`), NOT at `n = 0`.
192	
193	**An independent confirmation that `+g` is the right target**, worth recording because the
194	wrong sign survived two sessions: at `deg W = g` the rank anchor
195	`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives, for a
196	witness with `h¹ = 0`,
197	`h⁰ = deg W + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1` — exactly the `h⁰ = 1` normalization that DAT-C §2 and
198	GAP-2's uniqueness both require.  So `+g` is not merely the sign that makes the locus nonempty;
199	it is the unique degree at which the witness is *unique*, which is what the chart map needs to be
200	injective.  At `−g` the same anchor gives `h⁰ = 1 − 2g`, negative for `g ≥ 1` — the contradiction
201	that made the locus empty. -/
202	theorem degAt_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
203	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T)
204	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
205	    degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
206	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
207	  rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
208	    degAt_sigmaFamily, (mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hlam) K t]
209	  ring
210	
211	/-- **`chartTwist` inverts `chartValue`'s twist** — the sign check, as a theorem rather than a
212	docstring claim.
213	
214	Applying `chartTwist` to a chart value returns the Abel class it came from.  This is the
215	statement that was FALSE of the earlier definition (which returned
216	`abelDiv · Σ² · (θᵐ)⁻²`), and it is why the direction is now pinned by the kernel: any future
217	edit to `chartTwist` that breaks the inversion breaks this lemma.
218	
219	Recorded per issue I-0514.  A degree ledger alone does not catch a sign error — the wrong-signed
220	ledger was internally consistent — but an inversion law does. -/
221	theorem chartTwist_chartValue {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ)
222	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
223	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
224	    chartTwist C m Z T (chartValue C π n m Z T s) = abelDiv C π n T s := by
225	  rw [chartTwist, chartValue]
226	  group
227	
228	/-! ## CHART-U(a): the locus -/
229	
230	variable (C) in
231	/-- **CHART-U(a), `chartLocus`** (`w4-datc` §3.3, co-signed `w4-datb` §1.6): the set of
232	points of a general test `T` at which the twisted fibre class `λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)` has, after
233	some finite separable splitting of the collapsed plus class at `κ(t)`, an effective witness
234	divisor with vanishing `H¹`.

87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
88	
89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
101	
102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
103	
104	variable (C) in
105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
106	
107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
110	
111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
119	
120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
123	
124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
134	  intro T s
135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
137	
138	variable (C) in
139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
140	
141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
152	
153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
154	
155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
161	
162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
165	
166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
186	
187	end

1	/-

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance
8	
9	/-!
10	# C9b: `IsChartUniv` reduced to one clause about the chart locus
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` splits `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` into the two
13	clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
14	input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
15	`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
16	
17	The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:
20	
21	| field | at the Abel chart | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
24	  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
25	| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
26	| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
27	| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |
28	
29	So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
30	`r` is, and the genuine content is
31	concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
32	GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
33	exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
34	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.
35	
36	## Why this is not a restatement
37	
38	A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
39	that failure mode in two directions:
40	
41	* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane
42	  no longer has to invent.
43	
44	  **RETRACTED 2026-07-29, second clause only** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  This
45	  read "the `W` field costs zero, which is a real reduction of the datum from four fields to
46	  three".  The cost is not zero: `chartLocusOpens` takes the argument `haff`, and **nothing in
47	  the tree discharges it**.  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` removed the
48	  `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis but passes `haff` straight through, as does
49	  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it; the affine case that would feed it
50	  (`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`) is itself conditional on
51	  `IsChartDatumPresentation`, which is dat-b row B-4's named residue and is only half landed.
52	  So the datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  The
53	  residue is now named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4's own obligation by
54	  `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`;
55	* `isChartLocusFibre_of_isChartUniv` is the **converse**: `IsChartUniv` at the chart locus
56	  gives injectivity on every test, so a lane cannot obtain `IsChartUniv` while avoiding the
57	  content of `exists_factor`.  The reduction is therefore an equivalence in the direction
58	  that matters, not a weakening.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens` — `chartLocus` as an honest `T.Opens`, using the
63	  unconditional general-test openness.  This is the `V` that `restrictChart` wants.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartLocusFibre` — the residue: the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple
65	  of the criterion, at the chart locus, for every test point.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` — **the reduction**: that triple
67	  gives `IsChartUniv` (hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)` pair) at any open.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isChartUniv` — the converse-direction check.
69	-/
70	
71	set_option autoImplicit false
72	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
73	
74	universe u
75	
76	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
77	
78	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
79	
80	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
82	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
83	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
84	
85	noncomputable section
86	
87	/-! ## The chart locus as an open of the test
88	
89	`chartLocus` is a `Set T.left` and `restrictChart` wants a `T.Opens`.  The bridge is the
90	openness theorem.  **"which is now unconditional — so this costs a hypothesis-free definition
91	rather than a gate" is RETRACTED** (2026-07-29): the general-test openness theorem is
92	unconditional in `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` but still takes the affine-local `haff`, which
93	nothing discharges.  See `chartLocusOpens`' docstring and
94	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`. -/
95	
96	variable (C) in
97	/-- **`chartLocus` as an open subscheme of the test.**
98	
99	For a test `T` presented as `Over.mk a` and a class `lam` on it, the chart locus is open by
100	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (CHART-U(b) at a general test, unconditional since
101	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged), so it is an honest element of `T.Opens`.
102	
103	**THE `haff` SENTENCE HERE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED** (2026-07-29,
104	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  It read: "The `haff` hypothesis is the affine-local
105	input of that theorem and is *not* a residue of this file: it is what the landed affine
106	openness supplies."  The landed affine openness does **not** supply it.
107	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`) is conditional
108	on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — dat-b row B-4's own named residue, whose *witness* half is now
109	discharged too (`hconv`, by plus-unit injectivity,
110	`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`), leaving a plus-class base-change
111	identity — and no theorem in the tree produces `haff` for a general test.  It is a genuine
112	open obligation, named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4 by
113	`chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`.  It is
114	carried as an argument here so the definition does not silently depend on a chosen route. -/
115	def chartLocusOpens (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
116	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
117	    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
118	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :
119	    T.left.Opens where
120	  carrier := chartLocus C m Z lam
121	  is_open' := isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal' C m Z T lam haff
122	
123	@[simp]
124	lemma mem_chartLocusOpens {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
125	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T}
126	    {haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
127	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))}
128	    {t : T.left} :
129	    t ∈ chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
130	  Iff.rfl
131	
132	/-! ## The residue, named -/
133	
134	variable (C π n) in
135	/-- **The residue of C9b, named**: for every test point of the Σ-sheaf, the chart point over
136	its chart locus together with the two properties the criterion needs.
137	
138	This is `ChartFibrePresented` with its `W` field already discharged — it is `chartLocus`,
139	open unconditionally — so what a lane owes is precisely:
140	
141	* `r`: the divisor family over the locus whose class is the given one.  This is the
142	  classifier `divRepClassifyZar` applied to the canonical-section family, i.e. CHART-U(c)'s
143	  construction;
144	* `sq`: that its chart value *is* the given class, which is the classifier's characterising
145	  property;
146	* `exists_factor`: that two points with the same class agree, i.e. the **relative form of
147	  DAT-C GAP-2** (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` in families).
148	
149	Stated as a `Prop` over an arbitrary presenting datum rather than as a structure carrying the
150	family, because the family is the classifier's output and this lane must not guess its shape:
151	the existential is over morphisms of schemes only. -/
152	def IsChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
153	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
154	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
155	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) : Prop :=
156	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
157	    Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) g)
158	
159	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: the residue above gives `IsChartUniv`, hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)`
160	pair, at *any* open of the divisor scheme.
161	
162	Two things are worth reading off the proof.  First, it goes through the criterion of
163	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` and then through the *composition* half
164	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` already landed in `Pic0ChartPair.lean` — so the two
165	halves of C9b compose exactly as the file headers predicted, with no seam.  Second, the open
166	`V` is arbitrary: restriction never has to be to the chart locus for `hf` to hold, because
167	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is stable under precomposition with an open immersion.  The chart
168	locus is where the *unrestricted* statement becomes true, which is a statement about
169	`IsChartLocusFibre`, not about `V`. -/
170	theorem isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
171	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
172	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
173	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
174	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
175	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) (V : D.left.Opens) :
176	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
177	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V
178	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some)

165	variable (C) in
166	/-- **The twisted family whose chart-membership `chartLocus` tests**: the plus class `λ`
167	shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family.

169	This is the *class-side* half of `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`): where
170	`chartValue` twists the Abel class of a divisor family, `chartTwist` twists an arbitrary
171	plus class by the same two factors.  A point of `chartLocus` is precisely a point at which

173	a chart value, after undoing the twist. -/
174	def chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : picEt C T :=
176	  lam * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m) * (sigmaFamily C Z T)⁻¹
177	
178	/-- **The degree ledger of the twist**: at every field point the twisted family has fibre
179	degree `m·d₁ − deg Z` when `λ` is degree-zero.  With the chart-index constraint
180	`deg Z = m·d₁ − g` this is `+g`, which is the degree at which an effective witness with
181	`h¹ = 0` can exist at all.

183	**Sign discipline, and it was wrong here until 2026-07-28 (issue I-0514).**  `chartTwist`
184	must be the INVERSE of `chartValue`'s twist, not the same one.  `chartValue` is
185	`abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`), so recovering the Abel class from a chart
186	value means multiplying by `θᵐ` and dividing by `Σ` — hence `chartTwist` is
187	`λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`.  An earlier version applied the `chartValue` twist itself, giving fibre degree
188	`deg Z − m·d₁ = −g`; since `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))` forces `deg W ≥ g − 1`, that locus was
189	**empty for every `g ≥ 1`** and its openness was the openness of `∅`.  The comparison point is
190	`degAt_chartValue` at `n = g` (where the chart index is calibrated and `chartValue` lands in
191	`pic0`), NOT at `n = 0`.

197	`h⁰ = deg W + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1` — exactly the `h⁰ = 1` normalization that DAT-C §2 and

199	it is the unique degree at which the witness is *unique*, which is what the chart map needs to be
200	injective.  At `−g` the same anchor gives `h⁰ = 1 − 2g`, negative for `g ≥ 1` — the contradiction

203	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T)
204	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
205	    degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
206	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
207	  rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
208	    degAt_sigmaFamily, (mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hlam) K t]

237	* the *point-to-field-point* passage is `Over.testPoint` (input 0 of this brick — the one

244	def chartLocus (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)

246	  {t : T.left | IsSplitWitness C

126	## A convention this predicate INHERITS, and which a consumer must not misread

138	Two consequences, both load-bearing:

140	* the degree is supplied **externally**, by the chart-index constraint through

143	  hypothesis of this predicate.  (Until 2026-07-28 this read `−g`, and that sign made the
144	  locus empty for every `g ≥ 1` — see `degAt_chartTwist` and issue I-0514;

146	* effectivity likewise is not asserted here.  Where the *worksheet's* stronger reading is

166	/-- **The twisted family whose chart-membership `chartLocus` tests**: the plus class `λ`
167	shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family.
168	
169	This is the *class-side* half of `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`): where
170	`chartValue` twists the Abel class of a divisor family, `chartTwist` twists an arbitrary
171	plus class by the same two factors.  A point of `chartLocus` is precisely a point at which
172	`chartTwist` is realised by an effective divisor with no `H¹` — i.e. at which `λ` itself is
173	a chart value, after undoing the twist. -/
174	def chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : picEt C T :=
176	  lam * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m) * (sigmaFamily C Z T)⁻¹
177	
178	/-- **The degree ledger of the twist**: at every field point the twisted family has fibre
179	degree `m·d₁ − deg Z` when `λ` is degree-zero.  With the chart-index constraint
180	`deg Z = m·d₁ − g` this is `+g`, which is the degree at which an effective witness with
181	`h¹ = 0` can exist at all.
182	
183	**Sign discipline, and it was wrong here until 2026-07-28 (issue I-0514).**  `chartTwist`
184	must be the INVERSE of `chartValue`'s twist, not the same one.  `chartValue` is
185	`abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`), so recovering the Abel class from a chart
186	value means multiplying by `θᵐ` and dividing by `Σ` — hence `chartTwist` is
187	`λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`.  An earlier version applied the `chartValue` twist itself, giving fibre degree
188	`deg Z − m·d₁ = −g`; since `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))` forces `deg W ≥ g − 1`, that locus was
189	**empty for every `g ≥ 1`** and its openness was the openness of `∅`.  The comparison point is
190	`degAt_chartValue` at `n = g` (where the chart index is calibrated and `chartValue` lands in
191	`pic0`), NOT at `n = 0`.

193	**An independent confirmation that `+g` is the right target**, worth recording because the
194	wrong sign survived two sessions: at `deg W = g` the rank anchor
195	`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives, for a
196	witness with `h¹ = 0`,
197	`h⁰ = deg W + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1` — exactly the `h⁰ = 1` normalization that DAT-C §2 and
198	GAP-2's uniqueness both require.  So `+g` is not merely the sign that makes the locus nonempty;
199	it is the unique degree at which the witness is *unique*, which is what the chart map needs to be
200	injective.  At `−g` the same anchor gives `h⁰ = 1 − 2g`, negative for `g ≥ 1` — the contradiction
201	that made the locus empty. -/
202	theorem degAt_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)

204	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
205	    degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
206	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
207	  rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
208	    degAt_sigmaFamily, (mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hlam) K t]
209	  ring

219	Recorded per issue I-0514.  A degree ledger alone does not catch a sign error — the wrong-signed
220	ledger was internally consistent — but an inversion law does. -/
221	theorem chartTwist_chartValue {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ)
222	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))

9	/-!
10	# C9b: the restricted chart map and the `(f, hf)` pair
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds the Abel chart map `abelSigmaChart` out of a
13	representation of the divisor functor, and its header states — correctly — that
14	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
15	scheme**: the Abel map has projective spaces `|D|` as fibres, so it is not even a
16	monomorphism.  It becomes an open immersion only after restriction to the locus where the
17	fibre is a single point.
18	
19	This file supplies the restriction, which is the half of C9b that needs no new mathematics
20	once `chartLocus` exists — and it makes precise which half does.
21	
22	## What C9b consists of, and which part is here
23	
24	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) consumes a pair
25	`(f, hf)`.  Producing it from `abelSigmaChart` factors into exactly two steps:
26	
27	1. **restrict the source along an open immersion** — `restrictChart` below.  Given any open
28	   `V ⊆ D.left`, precomposing `abelSigmaChart` with `yoneda.map V.ι` gives a chart map out of
29	   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.
30	2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.
31	   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:
32	   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.
33	   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free
34	   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +
35	   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the
36	   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.
37	   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the
38	   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).
39	
40	So: the *composition* half of the `hf` certificate is discharged here, unconditionally; the
41	*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the
42	classifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).
43	
44	## CORRECTION 2026-07-29: step 2 above is itself TWO clauses, not one
45	
46	The description of step 2 as "*the* honest content" is right that it is not bookkeeping and
47	wrong that it is a single obligation.  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` conjoins **relative
48	representability** (the fibre product is a scheme at all) with **the property clause** (each
49	represented pullback is an open immersion).  The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to the
50	second only.  The first needs just an open of the test, and `chartLocus` is one
51	unconditionally — so it is not CERT-Σ-gated at all.
52	
53	That split is landed: `Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` (the criterion, from
54	elementwise data) and `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` (instantiated at the Abel chart,
55	reducing the datum from four fields to three).  `IsChartUniv` below is unchanged as a
56	*statement* — it is still the right pin — but it is no longer the right unit of *pricing*.
57	Read `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` for what a lane now actually owes.
58	
59	## Main declarations
60	
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` — an open immersion of schemes is
62	  an open immersion of presheaves under yoneda.  This is mathlib's `relative_map` at
63	  `P := IsOpenImmersion`, recorded once with the instances it needs discharged.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictChart` — the chart map restricted to an open of the source.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` — **the composition half of
66	  `hf`**: if the unrestricted chart map is an open immersion of presheaves, so is any
67	  restriction of it along an open immersion.  Unconditional in the restriction.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_restrictChart` — the structure morphism of a restricted chart
69	  is the restriction of the structure morphism, so the `LocallyOfFiniteType` hypothesis of
70	  `JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited (being locally of finite type is local on the
71	  source).
72	-/

variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))

/-- **The chart atlas of `DivScheme g`** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.3): each
`Z(♦)`-chart `Spec R_Z` maps to `DivScheme g`, factoring the chart presentation through
`divSchemeι`.  The kill law is `divCarveIdeal_le_ker_of_tower` at the chart ring itself
(spelled `Ideal.mk_ker`). -/
noncomputable def divCarveChartToDivScheme
    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
    Spec (CommRingCat.of (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j))
      ⟶ DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ :=
  carveLocusToCarveScheme k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j

/-- **The defining triangle of the `DivScheme` chart atlas**: through the closed immersion
`divSchemeι`, the chart map of `Spec R_Z` is `Spec` of the quotient presentation
`divCarveChartMk` followed by the pair chart. -/
theorem divCarveChartToDivScheme_divSchemeι
    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
    divCarveChartToDivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j ≫ divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (divCarveChartMk k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j).toRingHom)
        ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j :=
  carveLocusToCarveScheme_carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j

/-- **The atlas factorization of `DivScheme g`** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.3,
the DDR-9.F1 keystone): every test morphism `v : overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver` factors,
over a finite spanning family of basic localizations of `S`, through some chart
`divCarveChartToDivScheme i j` along a `k`-algebra map
`ω : R_Z →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t)` out of the `Z(♦)`-chart ring. -/
theorem divScheme_exists_chartFactor (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → S), Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ t : Fin m, ∃ (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
        (ω : DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t)),
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ω.toRingHom)
            ≫ divCarveChartToDivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j
          = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S (Localization.Away (f t))))
            ≫ v.left :=
  carveScheme_exists_chartFactor k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) S v

end Curve

section PairChart

open CategoryTheory Limits

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] (d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂ : ℕ)

/-- The chart ring of the Grassmannian pair at a pair of chart indices:
`R_{I,J} = R^I ⊗[k] R^J`. -/
abbrev PairChartRing (i : (glueData k d₁ r₁).J) (j : (glueData k d₂ r₂).J) : Type u :=
  TensorProduct k (ChartRing k d₁ r₁ i.down.1) (ChartRing k d₂ r₂ j.down.1)

/-- The affine pair chart of the Grassmannian pair:
`Spec (R^I ⊗[k] R^J) ⟶ grPair`, the `grPairPatchIso`-twisted patch inclusion of the
product atlas `grPairCover`. -/
noncomputable def pairChartMap (i : (glueData k d₁ r₁).J) (j : (glueData k d₂ r₂).J) :
    Spec (CommRingCat.of (PairChartRing k d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂ i j)) ⟶ grPair k d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂ :=
  (grPairPatchIso k d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂ i j).inv ≫ (grPairCover k d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂).f (i, j)

instance isOpenImmersion_pairChartMap (i : (glueData k d₁ r₁).J) (j : (glueData k d₂ r₂).J) :
    IsOpenImmersion (pairChartMap k d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂ i j) := by
  haveI h1 := (grPairCover k d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂).map_prop (i, j)
  exact @IsOpenImmersion.comp _ _ _ (grPairPatchIso k d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂ i j).inv
    ((grPairCover k d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂).f (i, j)) inferInstance h1

/-- The first projection of a pair chart: through `grPairFst`, the pair chart maps to the
chart `U^I` of the first Grassmannian by the left inclusion `R^I → R^I ⊗ R^J`. -/
theorem pairChartMap_fst (i : (glueData k d₁ r₁).J) (j : (glueData k d₂ r₂).J) :
    pairChartMap k d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂ i j ≫ grPairFst k d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂
      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := k)
            (A := ChartRing k d₁ r₁ i.down.1) (B := ChartRing k d₂ r₂ j.down.1)))
        ≫ (glueData k d₁ r₁).ι i := by
  have hcov : (grPairCover k d₁ r₁ d₂ r₂).f (i, j) ≫
        Limits.pullback.fst (grStructMap k d₁ r₁) (grStructMap k d₂ r₂)
      = Limits.pullback.fst ((glueData k d₁ r₁).openCover.f i ≫ grStructMap k d₁ r₁)
          ((glueData k d₂ r₂).openCover.f j ≫ grStructMap k d₂ r₂)

namespace MorphismProperty

open Functor.relativelyRepresentable

variable {X Y : D} (P : MorphismProperty C)

/-- Given a morphism property `P` in a category `C`, a functor `F : C ⥤ D` and a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` in `D`. Then `f` satisfies the morphism property `P.relative` with respect to `F` iff:
* The morphism is representable with respect to `F`
* For any morphism `g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, the property `P` holds for any represented pullback of
  `f` by `g`. -/
def relative : MorphismProperty D :=
  fun X Y f ↦ F.relativelyRepresentable f ∧
    ∀ ⦃a b : C⦄ (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y) (fst : F.obj b ⟶ X) (snd : b ⟶ a)
      (_ : IsPullback fst (F.map snd) f g), P snd

/-- Given a morphism property `P` in a category `C`, a morphism `f : F ⟶ G` of presheaves in the
category `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` satisfies the morphism property `P.presheaf` iff:
* The morphism is representable.
* For any morphism `g : F.obj a ⟶ G`, the property `P` holds for any represented pullback of
  `f` by `g`.

This is implemented as a special case of the more general notion of `P.relative`, to the case when
the functor `F` is `yoneda`. -/
abbrev presheaf : MorphismProperty (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) := P.relative yoneda

variable {P} {F}

/-- A morphism satisfying `P.relative` is representable. -/
lemma relative.rep {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : P.relative F f) : F.relativelyRepresentable f :=
  hf.1

lemma relative.property {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : P.relative F f) :
    ∀ ⦃a b : C⦄ (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y) (fst : F.obj b ⟶ X) (snd : b ⟶ a)
    (_ : IsPullback fst (F.map snd) f g), P snd :=
  hf.2

lemma relative.property_snd {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : P.relative F f) {a : C} (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y) :
    P (hf.rep.snd g) :=
  hf.property g _ _ (hf.rep.isPullback g)

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
/-- Given a morphism property `P` which respects isomorphisms, then to show that a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` satisfies `P.relative` it suffices to show that:
* The morphism is representable.
* For any morphism `g : F.obj a ⟶ G`, the property `P` holds for *some* represented pullback
  of `f` by `g`. -/
lemma relative.of_exists [F.Faithful] [F.Full] [P.RespectsIso] {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (h₀ : ∀ ⦃a : C⦄ (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y), ∃ (b : C) (fst : F.obj b ⟶ X) (snd : b ⟶ a)
      (_ : IsPullback fst (F.map snd) f g), P snd) : P.relative F f := by
  refine ⟨fun a g ↦ ?_, fun a b g fst snd h ↦ ?_⟩
  all_goals obtain ⟨c, g_fst, g_snd, BC, H⟩ := h₀ g
  · refine ⟨c, g_snd, g_fst, BC⟩
  · refine (P.arrow_mk_iso_iff ?_).2 H
    exact Arrow.isoMk (F.preimageIso (h.isoIsPullback X (F.obj a) BC)) (Iso.refl _)
      (F.map_injective (by simp))

lemma relative_of_snd [F.Faithful] [F.Full] [P.RespectsIso] {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : F.relativelyRepresentable f) (h : ∀ ⦃a : C⦄ (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y), P (hf.snd g)) :
    P.relative F f :=
  relative.of_exists (fun _ g ↦ ⟨hf.pullback g, hf.fst g, hf.snd g, hf.isPullback g, h g⟩)

/-- If `P : MorphismProperty C` is stable under base change, `F` is fully faithful and preserves
pullbacks, and `C` has all pullbacks, then for any `f : a ⟶ b` in `C`, `F.map f` satisfies
`P.relative` if `f` satisfies `P`. -/
lemma relative_map [F.Faithful] [F.Full] [HasPullbacks C] [IsStableUnderBaseChange P]
    {a b : C} {f : a ⟶ b} [∀ c (g : c ⟶ b), PreservesLimit (cospan f g) F]
    (hf : P f) : P.relative F (F.map f) := by
  apply relative.of_exists
  intro Y' g
  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := F.map_surjective g
  exact ⟨_, _, _, (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f g).map F, P.pullback_snd _ _ hf⟩

lemma of_relative_map {a b : C} {f : a ⟶ b} (hf : P.relative F (F.map f)) : P f :=
  hf.property (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) f (IsPullback.id_horiz (F.map f))

lemma relative_map_iff [F.Faithful] [F.Full] [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan F]
    [HasPullbacks C] [IsStableUnderBaseChange P] {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} :
    P.relative F (F.map f) ↔ P f :=
  ⟨fun hf ↦ of_relative_map hf, fun hf ↦ relative_map hf⟩

/-- If `P' : MorphismProperty C` is satisfied whenever `P` is, then also `P'.relative` is
satisfied whenever `P.relative` is. -/
lemma relative_monotone {P' : MorphismProperty C} (h : P ≤ P') :
    P.relative F ≤ P'.relative F := fun _ _ _ hf ↦
  ⟨hf.rep, fun _ _ g fst snd BC ↦ h _ (hf.property g fst snd BC)⟩

section

variable (P)

lemma relative_isStableUnderBaseChange : IsStableUnderBaseChange (P.relative F) where
  of_isPullback hfBC hg :=
    ⟨of_isPullback hfBC hg.rep,
      fun _ _ _ _ _ BC ↦ hg.property _ _ _ (IsPullback.paste_horiz BC hfBC)⟩

instance relative_isStableUnderComposition [F.Faithful] [F.Full] [P.IsStableUnderComposition] :
    IsStableUnderComposition (P.relative F) where
  comp_mem {F G H} f g hf hg := by
    refine ⟨comp_mem _ _ _ hf.1 hg.1, fun Z X p fst snd h ↦ ?_⟩
    rw [← hg.1.lift_snd (fst ≫ f) snd (by simpa using h.w)]
    refine comp_mem _ _ _ (hf.property (hg.1.fst p) fst _
      (IsPullback.of_bot ?_ ?_ (hg.1.isPullback p))) (hg.property_snd p)
    · rw [← Functor.map_comp, lift_snd]
      exact h
    · symm
      apply hg.1.lift_fst

instance relative_respectsIso : RespectsIso (P.relative F) :=
  (relative_isStableUnderBaseChange P).respectsIso

instance relative_isMultiplicative [F.Faithful] [F.Full] [P.IsMultiplicative] [P.RespectsIso] :
    IsMultiplicative (P.relative F) where
  id_mem X := relative.of_exists
    (fun Y g ↦ ⟨Y, g, 𝟙 Y, by simpa using IsPullback.of_id_snd, id_mem _ _⟩)

end

section

-- TODO(Calle): This could be generalized to functors whose image forms a separating family.
/-- Morphisms satisfying `(monomorphism C).presheaf` are in particular monomorphisms. -/
lemma presheaf_monomorphisms_le_monomorphisms :
    (monomorphisms C).presheaf ≤ monomorphisms _ := fun F G f hf ↦ by
  suffices ∀ {X : C} {a b : yoneda.obj X ⟶ F}, a ≫ f = b ≫ f → a = b from
    ⟨fun _ _ h ↦ hom_ext_yoneda (fun _ _ ↦ this (by simp only [assoc, h]))⟩
  intro X a b h
  /- It suffices to show that the lifts of `a` and `b` to morphisms
  `X ⟶ hf.rep.pullback g` are equal, where `g = a ≫ f = a ≫ f`. -/
  suffices hf.rep.lift (g := a ≫ f) a (𝟙 X) (by simp) =
      hf.rep.lift b (𝟙 X) (by simp [← h]) by
    simpa using yoneda.congr_map this =≫ (hf.rep.fst (a ≫ f))
  -- This follows from the fact that the induced maps `hf.rep.pullback g ⟶ X` are mono.
  have : Mono (hf.rep.snd (a ≫ f)) := hf.property_snd (a ≫ f)
  simp only [← cancel_mono (hf.rep.snd (a ≫ f)), lift_snd]

variable {G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁}

lemma presheaf_mono_of_le (hP : P ≤ MorphismProperty.monomorphisms C)
    {X : C} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ G} (hf : P.presheaf f) : Mono f :=
  MorphismProperty.presheaf_monomorphisms_le_monomorphisms _
    (MorphismProperty.relative_monotone hP _ hf)

lemma fst'_self_eq_snd (hP : P ≤ MorphismProperty.monomorphisms C)
    {X : C} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ G} (hf : P.presheaf f) : hf.rep.fst' f = hf.rep.snd f := by
  have := P.presheaf_mono_of_le hP hf
  apply yoneda.map_injective
  rw [← cancel_mono f, (hf.rep.isPullback' f).w]

lemma isIso_fst'_self (hP : P ≤ MorphismProperty.monomorphisms C)
    {X : C} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ G} (hf : P.presheaf f) : IsIso (hf.rep.fst' f) :=
  have := P.presheaf_mono_of_le hP hf
  have := (hf.rep.isPullback' f).isIso_fst_of_mono
  Yoneda.fullyFaithful.isIso_of_isIso_map _

end

end MorphismProperty

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartTwistCollapse

/-!
# A plus class becomes honest over its own étale carrier — over an ARBITRARY affine base

This closes the obligation the CHART-U(b) header table names "honesty over a general affine
base" (issue I-0558), and it needs no field.

## The obligation, and why it looked hard

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean`'s route needs a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over an affine base
whose class is the (collapsed) twisted class.  `exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass`
(`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`) supplies the datum — but it takes an **honest Čech
class** `c` over the base as a *hypothesis*, and a plus class over `Spec A` is not honest: it is
`PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E` of `A`.

The tree's only route from a plus class to an honest one was
`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s `exists_splitting_of_picEt`, which requires `[Field K]` — its
engine is étale field-cofinality (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`),
false over a general base.  So the obligation read as: find a *substitute* for cofinality over
`Spec A`.

## Why it is in fact free

There is no substitute needed, because **a cover splits over its own carrier**.  The
field-cofinality theorem is used to produce an `A`-algebra map `E.Carrier →ₐ L` into something
where the class becomes a unit; but the identity `E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier` is already such a
map, and it exists for every cover over every base.  Restricting the plus class along
`A → E.Carrier` therefore makes it honest, with no finiteness, separability, or field
hypothesis anywhere.

Concretely `PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x` — the
transported class is presented by `x` itself.  The proof is the general-base analogue of
`PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom` (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`), which is stated
only for fields; the field hypotheses there are inherited from *its* consumer (the degree seam,
which reads a degree and so needs a field), not required by the argument.  The one substantive
step is the same in both: the descent condition `x.2`, fed to `relPicAlgMap_congr`, identifies
the two ways of transporting `x` to the base-changed carrier.

## What this does and does not give

It gives honesty **over `Spec E.Carrier`**, not over `Spec A`.  That is exactly what the
(b-amendment) asks for — its step is "over the étale carrier `B := E.Carrier` the class is
honest", after which the engine fires on `Spec B` and transport (ii) pushes the open locus down
to `Spec A` along the (open, surjective) carrier map.  Nothing here performs that descent; the
topological core of it is landed as `isOpen_of_isOpen_comap_preimage`
(`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean:129`).

So after this file the CHART-U(b) route has ONE remaining obligation, the pointwise
`IsChartDatumPresentation` — and, unlike the previous "one remaining obligation" claims on this
lane, that one is a genuine statement about matching two fibre predicates, not a missing
construction.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self` — **a plus class is honest over its own
  cover carrier**, over an arbitrary affine base.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_honest_of_picEtAff` — the existential form.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_cechPicClass_twist` — the payoff, in the engine's shape: over
  a base where the class is honest, a datum presenting it twisted by any chart index exists.
-/

public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Representable
public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.BigZariski

public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.GluingOneHypercover

/-!
# Representability of schemes is a local property

In this file we prove that a sheaf of types `F` on `Sch` is representable if it is
locally representable.

## Main result
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresentability.isRepresentable`:
  Suppose
  * F is a `Type u`-valued sheaf on `Sch` with respect to the Zariski topology
  * X : ι → Sch is a family of schemes
  * f : Π i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ F is a family of relatively representable open immersions
  * f is jointly surjective

  Then `F` is representable.

## References
* https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01JJ

-/

@[expose] public section

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open CategoryTheory Category Limits Opposite

universe u

namespace Scheme

/-
Consider the following setup:
* F is `Type u`-valued a sheaf on `Sch` with respect to the Zariski topology
* X : ι → Sch is a family of schemes
* f : Π i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ F is a family of relatively representable open immersions

Later, we will also assume:
* The family f is locally surjective with respect to the Zariski topology
-/
variable (F : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u))
  {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
  (f : (i : ι) → yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ F.1) (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))

namespace LocalRepresentability

variable {F f} (i j k : ι)

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
open Functor.relativelyRepresentable in
/-- We get a family of gluing data by taking `U i = X i` and `V i j = (hf i).rep.pullback (f j)`. -/
@[simps]
noncomputable def glueData : GlueData where
  J := ι
  U := X
  V := fun (i, j) ↦ (hf i).rep.pullback (f j)
  f i j := (hf i).rep.fst' (f j)
  f_mono i j :=
    have := (hf j).property _ _ _ ((hf i).1.isPullback' (f j)).flip
    IsOpenImmersion.mono _
  f_id i := IsOpenImmersion.isIso_fst'_self IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms (hf i)
  t i j := (hf i).rep.symmetry (hf j).rep
  t_id i := by apply (hf i).rep.hom_ext' <;>
    simp [IsOpenImmersion.fst'_self_eq_snd IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms (hf i)]
  t' i j k := lift₃ _ _ _ (pullback₃.p₂ _ _ _) (pullback₃.p₃ _ _ _) (pullback₃.p₁ _ _ _)
    (by simp) (by simp)
  t_fac i j k := (hf j).rep.hom_ext' (by simp) (by simp)
  cocycle i j k := pullback₃.hom_ext (by simp) (by simp) (by simp)
  f_open i j := (hf j).property _ _ _ ((hf i).1.isPullback' (f j)).flip

/-- The map from `X i` to the glued scheme `(glueData hf).glued` -/
noncomputable def toGlued (i : ι) : X i ⟶ (glueData hf).glued :=
  (glueData hf).ι i

instance : IsOpenImmersion (toGlued hf i) :=
  inferInstanceAs (IsOpenImmersion ((glueData hf).ι i))

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- The map from the glued scheme `(glueData hf).glued`, treated as a sheaf, to `F`. -/
noncomputable def yonedaGluedToSheaf :
    zariskiTopology.yoneda.obj (glueData hf).glued ⟶ F where
  -- The map is obtained by finding an object of `F((glueData hf).glued)`.
  hom := yonedaEquiv.symm
  -- This section is obtained from gluing the section corresponding to `f i : Hom(-, X i) ⟶ F`.
    ((glueData hf).sheafValGluedMk (fun i ↦ yonedaEquiv (f i)) (by
      intro i j
      apply yonedaEquiv.symm.injective
      dsimp only [glueData_V, glueData_J, glueData_U, glueData_f, glueData_t]
      rw [yonedaEquiv_naturality, Equiv.symm_apply_apply,
        Functor.map_comp_apply, yonedaEquiv_naturality, yonedaEquiv_naturality,
        Equiv.symm_apply_apply, ← Functor.map_comp_assoc,
        Functor.relativelyRepresentable.symmetry_fst, ((hf i).rep.isPullback' (f j)).w]))

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma yoneda_toGlued_yonedaGluedToSheaf (i : ι) :
    yoneda.map (toGlued hf i) ≫ (yonedaGluedToSheaf hf).hom = f i := by
  apply yonedaEquiv.injective
  rw [yonedaGluedToSheaf, yonedaEquiv_apply, yonedaEquiv_apply,
    NatTrans.comp_app_apply, yoneda_map_app]
  simpa using! GlueData.sheafValGluedMk_val _ _ _ _

@[simp]
lemma yonedaGluedToSheaf_app_toGlued {i : ι} :

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartPair
7	
8	/-!
9	# C9b: what `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` of a chart map actually asks for
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` pins `IsChartUniv` — the `hf` half of the `(f, hf)` pair that
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes — and its docstring, together with the `c9b` roadmap
13	row, prices it as **one** obligation: the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 plus the classifier,
14	CERT-Σ-gated.
15	
16	**That pricing is wrong, and this file is the correction.**  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is
17	`MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda` (mathlib `MorphismProperty/Representable.lean`), and
18	`relative` is *by definition* a conjunction of two independent statements:
19	
20	1. **relative representability** — for every test `T` and every `g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ 𝓟`, the
21	   fibre product of the chart map along `g` is representable *by a scheme*;
22	2. **the property clause** — every represented pullback is an open immersion of schemes.
23	
24	The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to (2) only: it is what makes the fibre a single
25	point, hence the represented pullback an open subscheme.  It says nothing about (1), which
26	is a representability statement about a fibre product.  Read as one clause, a lane waits on
27	CERT-Σ for both halves.  Read as two, half of the work is stateable and provable *now*, with
28	no divisor-representability endpoint and no certificate anywhere in it.
29	
30	## What this file provides, and what it deliberately does not
31	
32	Everything here is stated for an **arbitrary** morphism of big-site presheaves
33	`f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` and an **arbitrary** open `V ⊆ X`.  No `divRep`
34	endpoint, no certificate, no `Z`, no `θ` and no chart index appears in any statement.  That
35	is the point: `IsChartUniv` becomes *this criterion instantiated at* `abelSigmaChart`, and
36	the divisor-representability shape enters only at the instantiation.
37	
38	The criterion's hypotheses are **elementwise** conditions on the presheaf — a fibrewise
39	injectivity clause and a clause producing the representing open — because that is what
40	mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists` reduces the goal to once the presheaf
41	category's pullbacks are computed pointwise (`Types.isPullback_iff`).
42	
43	## Main declarations
44	
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartFibrePresented` — the elementwise datum (1) needs: for each test
46	  point `g` of the target, an open `W` of the test and an identification of the `W`-points
47	  with the chart points hitting `g`.  This is the *shape* of a fibre-product presentation,
48	  named so that a producer knows exactly what it owes.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` — **the criterion**:
50	  a `ChartFibrePresented` datum gives `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f`, discharging BOTH clauses
51	  at once.  Certificate-free and divRep-free.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the converse direction that makes
53	  the split honest: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` *implies* `f` is a monomorphism.  So "the
54	  Abel map is not a monomorphism", which three files cite as the reason the unrestricted
55	  certificate fails, is a consequence of the criterion rather than an extra obligation — and
56	  it shows the elementwise injectivity clause below is **necessary**, not an artefact of
57	  this route.
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the same fact in the
59	  elementwise form a chart-locus argument can actually use.
60	-/
61	
62	set_option autoImplicit false
63	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
64	
65	universe u
66	
67	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
68	
69	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
70	
71	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
72	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
73	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
74	
75	noncomputable section
76	
77	/-! ## The necessary direction: an open immersion of presheaves is a monomorphism
78	
79	Stated first, because it is what tells us the criterion below asks for the right thing. -/
80	
81	/-- **An open immersion of presheaves out of a representable is a monomorphism.**
82	
83	This is mathlib's `presheaf_mono_of_le` at `P := IsOpenImmersion`, whose hypothesis
84	`IsOpenImmersion ≤ monomorphisms Scheme` is the landed `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.
85	
86	Recorded because the whole chart layer rests on the sentence "the Abel map is not a
87	monomorphism, so `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is false for the unrestricted divisor scheme"
88	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, repeated in `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`).  That sentence is a
89	*derivation*, not an independent input, and this lemma is the derivation. -/
90	theorem mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
91	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
92	    Mono f :=
93	  MorphismProperty.presheaf_mono_of_le IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms hf
94	
95	/-- **The elementwise form of the necessary direction**: if `f` is an open immersion of
96	presheaves then on every test it is injective on points.
97	
98	This is the clause `ChartFibrePresented.fibre_injective` below, read backwards, and it is
99	why that clause is not an artefact of this particular route: any proof of
100	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` whatsoever yields it.  For the Abel chart it is exactly "the
101	normalized effective representative is unique", i.e. the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 — so
102	GAP-2 is *forced* by the target, not merely sufficient for it. -/
103	theorem injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
104	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f)
105	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
106	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
107	  (mono_iff_injective (f.app T)).mp
108	    ((NatTrans.mono_iff_mono_app f).mp (mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf hf) T)
109	
110	/-! ## The sufficient direction: the elementwise datum, and the criterion -/
111	
112	variable (C) in
113	/-- **The fibre of a chart map over one test point, presented by an open of the test.**
114	
115	This is the datum mathlib's `relative.of_exists` asks for at a single
116	`g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C`, written out so a producer can see exactly what it
117	owes.  Given a chart map `f` out of `X`:
118	
119	* `W` is an open subscheme of the test `T` — the locus where the class named by `g` *is* a
120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;
123	* `exists_factor` is the honest content — a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with
124	  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;
125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
126	
127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
131	    where
132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
133	  W : T.Opens
134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
142	
143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
144	
145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
147	
148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
149	pullback of presheaves.
150	
151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
162	      φ.app S) D.sq
163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
168	    intro v w hvw
169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
171	
172	end ChartFibrePresented
173	
174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
176	
177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
178	is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
180	each.
181	
182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
184	
185	* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
187	* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
188	  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.
189	
190	What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
191	agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
192	form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the
193	classifier — so the CERT-Σ gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than
194	the whole certificate. -/
195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
197	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
198	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
199	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
200	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_
201	  exact ⟨(D T g).W, yoneda.map (D T g).r, (D T g).W.ι, (D T g).isPullback,
202	    inferInstance⟩
203	
204	/-! ## The criterion is not vacuous
205	
206	A structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a
207	criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
208	than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/

211	
212	If a chart map fails to be injective on the points of even one test, then no family of

229	normalized effective representative cannot supply the datum either — the CERT-Σ gate is not
230	an artefact of how `IsChartUniv` was pinned. -/

232	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
233	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
234	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
235	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
236	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
237	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T
238	
239	end
240	
241	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance
8	
9	/-!
10	# C9b: `IsChartUniv` reduced to one clause about the chart locus
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` splits `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` into the two
13	clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
14	input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
15	`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
16	
17	The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:
20	
21	| field | at the Abel chart | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
24	  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
25	| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
26	| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
27	| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |
28	
29	So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
30	`r` is, and the genuine content is
31	concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
32	GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
33	exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
34	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.
35	
36	## Why this is not a restatement
37	
38	A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
39	that failure mode in two directions:
40	
41	* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane
42	  no longer has to invent.
43	
44	  **RETRACTED 2026-07-29, second clause only** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  This
45	  read "the `W` field costs zero, which is a real reduction of the datum from four fields to
46	  three".  The cost is not zero: `chartLocusOpens` takes the argument `haff`, and **nothing in
47	  the tree discharges it**.  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` removed the
48	  `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis but passes `haff` straight through, as does
49	  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it; the affine case that would feed it
50	  (`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`) is itself conditional on
51	  `IsChartDatumPresentation`, which is dat-b row B-4's named residue and is only half landed.
52	  So the datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  The
53	  residue is now named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4's own obligation by
54	  `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`;
55	* `isChartLocusFibre_of_isChartUniv` is the **converse**: `IsChartUniv` at the chart locus
56	  gives injectivity on every test, so a lane cannot obtain `IsChartUniv` while avoiding the
57	  content of `exists_factor`.  The reduction is therefore an equivalence in the direction
58	  that matters, not a weakening.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens` — `chartLocus` as an honest `T.Opens`, using the
63	  unconditional general-test openness.  This is the `V` that `restrictChart` wants.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartLocusFibre` — the residue: the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple
65	  of the criterion, at the chart locus, for every test point.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` — **the reduction**: that triple
67	  gives `IsChartUniv` (hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)` pair) at any open.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isChartUniv` — the converse-direction check.
69	-/
70	
71	set_option autoImplicit false
72	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
73	
74	universe u
75	
76	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
77	
78	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
79	
80	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
82	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
83	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
84	
85	noncomputable section
86	
87	/-! ## The chart locus as an open of the test
88	
89	`chartLocus` is a `Set T.left` and `restrictChart` wants a `T.Opens`.  The bridge is the
90	openness theorem.  **"which is now unconditional — so this costs a hypothesis-free definition
91	rather than a gate" is RETRACTED** (2026-07-29): the general-test openness theorem is
92	unconditional in `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` but still takes the affine-local `haff`, which
93	nothing discharges.  See `chartLocusOpens`' docstring and
94	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`. -/
95	
96	variable (C) in
97	/-- **`chartLocus` as an open subscheme of the test.**
98	
99	For a test `T` presented as `Over.mk a` and a class `lam` on it, the chart locus is open by
100	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (CHART-U(b) at a general test, unconditional since
101	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged), so it is an honest element of `T.Opens`.
102	
103	**THE `haff` SENTENCE HERE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED** (2026-07-29,
104	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  It read: "The `haff` hypothesis is the affine-local
105	input of that theorem and is *not* a residue of this file: it is what the landed affine
106	openness supplies."  The landed affine openness does **not** supply it.
107	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`) is conditional
108	on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — dat-b row B-4's own named residue, whose *witness* half is now
109	discharged too (`hconv`, by plus-unit injectivity,
110	`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`), leaving a plus-class base-change
111	identity — and no theorem in the tree produces `haff` for a general test.  It is a genuine
112	open obligation, named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4 by
113	`chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`.  It is
114	carried as an argument here so the definition does not silently depend on a chosen route. -/
115	def chartLocusOpens (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
116	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
117	    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
118	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :
119	    T.left.Opens where
120	  carrier := chartLocus C m Z lam
121	  is_open' := isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal' C m Z T lam haff
122	
123	@[simp]
124	lemma mem_chartLocusOpens {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
125	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T}
126	    {haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
127	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))}
128	    {t : T.left} :
129	    t ∈ chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
130	  Iff.rfl
131	
132	/-! ## The residue, named -/
133	
134	variable (C π n) in
135	/-- **The residue of C9b, named**: for every test point of the Σ-sheaf, the chart point over
136	its chart locus together with the two properties the criterion needs.
137	
138	This is `ChartFibrePresented` with its `W` field already discharged — it is `chartLocus`,
139	open unconditionally — so what a lane owes is precisely:
140	
141	* `r`: the divisor family over the locus whose class is the given one.  This is the
142	  classifier `divRepClassifyZar` applied to the canonical-section family, i.e. CHART-U(c)'s
143	  construction;
144	* `sq`: that its chart value *is* the given class, which is the classifier's characterising
145	  property;
146	* `exists_factor`: that two points with the same class agree, i.e. the **relative form of
147	  DAT-C GAP-2** (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` in families).
148	
149	Stated as a `Prop` over an arbitrary presenting datum rather than as a structure carrying the
150	family, because the family is the classifier's output and this lane must not guess its shape:
151	the existential is over morphisms of schemes only. -/
152	def IsChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
153	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
154	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
155	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) : Prop :=
156	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
157	    Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) g)
158	
159	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: the residue above gives `IsChartUniv`, hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)`
160	pair, at *any* open of the divisor scheme.
161	
162	Two things are worth reading off the proof.  First, it goes through the criterion of
163	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` and then through the *composition* half
164	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` already landed in `Pic0ChartPair.lean` — so the two
165	halves of C9b compose exactly as the file headers predicted, with no seam.  Second, the open
166	`V` is arbitrary: restriction never has to be to the chart locus for `hf` to hold, because
167	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is stable under precomposition with an open immersion.  The chart
168	locus is where the *unrestricted* statement becomes true, which is a statement about
169	`IsChartLocusFibre`, not about `V`. -/
170	theorem isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
171	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
172	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
173	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
174	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
175	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) (V : D.left.Opens) :
176	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
177	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V
178	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some)
179	
180	/-! ## The converse check: the reduction is not a weakening -/
181	
182	/-- **`IsChartUniv` forces elementwise injectivity of the restricted chart.**
183	
184	The converse direction of the reduction, and the reason it is a reduction rather than a
185	restatement: a lane that obtains `IsChartUniv` has, for free, the injectivity statement that
186	`ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor` is the hard half of.  So there is no route to `hf` that
187	avoids relative GAP-2 — the gate is real, and this file has moved it rather than removed it.
188	
189	Compare `isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective`: that says the criterion cannot
190	be *satisfied* without injectivity; this says the goal cannot be *reached* without it. -/
191	theorem injective_of_isChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
192	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
193	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
194	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
195	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
196	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
197	    Function.Injective ((restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V).app T) :=
198	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf h T
199	
200	end
201	
202	end AlgebraicGeometry

local notation "DivOver" =>
  divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)

/-- The exact general-test data needed for the final F7 packaging.  In the intended
construction, `pull` is assembled from the affine forward maps and `classify` by
gluing the affine backward classifiers. -/
structure DivRepGlobalData where
  pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
    (T ⟶ DivOver) → divFamZar C pi g T
  classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
    divFamZar C pi g T → (T ⟶ DivOver)
  classify_pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver),
    classify (pull v) = v
  pull_classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T),
    pull (classify F) = F
  pull_comp : ∀ {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    (v : T ⟶ DivOver),
    pull (f ≫ v) = divFamZar.map C pi g f (pull v)

namespace DivRepGlobalData

/-- The general-test equivalence underlying the represented functor. -/
noncomputable def equiv
    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
    (T ⟶ DivOver) ≃ divFamZar C pi g T where
  toFun := D.pull
  invFun := D.classify
  left_inv := D.classify_pull
  right_inv := D.pull_classify

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
@[simp]
theorem equiv_apply

/-! ## Effective uniqueness -/

/-- **Effective uniqueness at `dim H⁰ = 1` (worker form)**: if `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`, the
classes agree, and the global sections of `𝒪(D)` are one-dimensional, then `D' = D`.
The extracted function realizing `D' − D` lies in `H⁰(𝒪(D))`, hence is a constant
multiple of `1 ∈ H⁰(𝒪(D))`, hence has trivial divisor. -/
theorem CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_finrank_one {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
    (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hD' : 0 ≤ D')
    (hcl : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D')
    (hone : Module.finrank K ↥(divisorSections K D ⊤) = 1) :
    D' = D := by
  -- the rational function with divisor `D' − D`
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq K hcl.symm
  -- `g ∈ H⁰(𝒪(D))`: `div g + D = D' ≥ 0`
  have hmem : (g : X.functionField) ∈ divisorSections K D ⊤ := by
    rw [mem_divisorSections_top_iff K g.ne_zero]
    have hmk : Units.mk0 (g : X.functionField) g.ne_zero = g := Units.ext rfl
    rw [hmk, ← hg, add_sub_cancel]
    exact hD'
  -- `h⁰ = 1` forces `g = c · 1`
  have h1mem : (1 : X.functionField) ∈ divisorSections K D ⊤ :=
    one_mem_divisorSections_top K hD
  have h1ne : (⟨1, h1mem⟩ : ↥(divisorSections K D ⊤)) ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    exact one_ne_zero (congrArg Subtype.val h)
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (finrank_eq_one_iff_of_nonzero' (⟨1, h1mem⟩ :
    ↥(divisorSections K D ⊤)) h1ne).mp hone ⟨(g : X.functionField), hmem⟩
  have hval : (g : X.functionField) = functionFieldOverAlgebraMap K X c := by
    have h : c • (1 : X.functionField) = (g : X.functionField) :=
      congrArg Subtype.val hc
    rw [← h, functionFieldOverModule_smul_def, mul_one]
  -- the constant has trivial divisor, so `D' − D = 0`
  have hdiv0 : Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g = 0 :=
    divOf_eq_zero_of_val_eq_functionFieldOverAlgebraMap K hval
  rw [hdiv0] at hg
  exact sub_eq_zero.mp hg

/-- **Effective uniqueness at `h⁰ = 1`** (worksheet GAP-2, Σ-UNIQ-fld — THE keystone):
an effective divisor `D` with `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1` is the unique effective representative of
its Čech Picard class. -/
theorem CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
    (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hD' : 0 ≤ D')
    (hcl : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D')
    (hone : Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) = 1) :
    D' = D :=
  CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_finrank_one K hD hD' hcl
    ((finrank_divisorSections_top K D).trans hone)
